comparisons.peer_summary: Operating expenses decreased 2% to $33.77 billion in 2024, aided by lower CIE commercial real estate impairments and prior year one-time charges like the GreenSky write-down, partially offset by higher compensation and transaction expenses, resulting in an efficiency ratio improvement to 63.1% from 74.6%.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze the drivers of operating/noninterest expense changes relative to the prior year, with both companies citing FDIC special assessments as a significant one-time or prior-year factor influencing the trend. BAC attributes its 2024 increase to organic growth in people/tech, partially offset by high 2023 FDIC costs ($2.1 billion). GS reports a decrease in operating expenses (2% lower) largely due to the absence of large prior-year impairments and a $529 million FDIC special assessment fee recognized in 2023, though GS also recognized an additional $71 million in 2024. Both filings highlight FDIC fees related to the SVB and Signature Bank closures as a critical variable in year-over-year comparisons, though BAC's net result was an expense increase while GS's was a decrease.

sentences.text: Noninterest expense increased $967 million to $66.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023.

The increase was primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology, partially offset by higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023, including $2.1 billion for the estimated special assessment amount arising from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.

Operating expenses were $33.77 billion for 2024, 2% lower than 2023, reflecting decreases driven by significantly lower expenses, including impairments, related to commercial real estate in consolidated investment entities (CIEs) and other significant expenses recognized in the prior year, including the write-down of identifiable intangible assets related to GreenSky Holdings, LLC (GreenSky), an impairment of goodwill related to Consumer platforms and the FDIC special assessment fee.
Our efficiency ratio (total operating expenses divided by total net revenues) was 63.1% for 2024, compared with 74.6% for 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense was $91.8 billion, up 5%, driven by higher compensation and a $1.0 billion Visa share contribution to the foundation, partially offset by lower FDIC-related expenses due to the timing of special assessments.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM report noninterest expense increases driven by higher compensation and revenue-related expenses, while both cite offsetting factors related to FDIC special assessments from previous bank closures. BAC reports a $967 million increase ($66.8 billion total) driven by investments in people and operations, partially offset by higher 2023 FDIC expenses ($2.1 billion special assessment). JPM reports a 5% increase ($91.8 billion total) driven by higher compensation and revenue-related pay, partially offset by lower FDIC-related expenses because the $2.9 billion special assessment was recognized in Q4 2023 compared to a smaller $725 million increase in Q1 2024. Both companies identify FDIC special assessments from SVB and Signature Bank closures as a key comparative driver, though BAC notes higher 2023 FDIC costs reducing the 2024 growth, while JPM notes lower 2024 FDIC costs relative to the large 2023 hit.

sentences.text: Noninterest expense increased $967 million to $66.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023.

The increase was primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology, partially offset by higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023, including $2.1 billion for the estimated special assessment amount arising from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.

• Noninterest expense was $91.8 billion, up 5%, driven by higher compensation expense, including higher revenue-related compensation and growth in the number of employees, as well as a $1.0 billion contribution of Visa shares to the JPMorgan Chase Foundation recorded in the second quarter of 2024, partially offset by lower FDIC-related expense, reflecting a $2.9 billion special assessment recognized in the fourth quarter of 2023, compared with a $725 million increase to the FDIC special assessment recognized in the first quarter of 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: Non-interest expenses totaled $19,129 million in 2024, a 5% increase year-over-year, driven by higher compensation and benefits (primarily discretionary incentive compensation) and higher non-compensation expenses (primarily execution-related and technology spend).
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS report increases in noninterest/non-compensation expenses driven by investments in people, compensation, and technology, while noting offsets from FDIC special assessment costs. BAC states expenses rose due to 'investments in people, operations and technology,' offset by 'higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023.' MS states non-interest expenses increased 5%, driven by 'higher Compensation and benefits expenses' and 'increased technology spend,' partially offset by 'lower FDIC special assessment cost.' Both companies link expense growth to personnel and technology investments and identify the prior-year FDIC burden as a comparative advantage in their current year's expense profile.

sentences.text: The increase was primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology, partially offset by higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023, including $2.1 billion for the estimated special assessment amount arising from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.
Non-interest expenses of $19,129 million in 2024 increased 5% compared with the prior year as a result of higher Non-compensation expenses and Compensation and benefits expenses.
• Compensation and benefits expenses increased primarily reflecting higher discretionary incentive compensation on higher revenues, partially offset by lower severance costs.

• Non-compensation expenses increased primarily reflecting higher execution-related expenses and increased technology spend, partially offset by lower legal expenses and lower FDIC special assessment cost.
